record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Are the following conditions equivalent: (1) S is right amenable; (2) S is right reversible; (3) for every A, B in S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}; (4) S contains no free subsemigroup of rank two; and (5) S is a subsemigroup of E(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Then the following conditions are equivalent. 1) The semigroup S is right amenable. 2) The semigroup S is right reversible. 3) For any two elements A, B of S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold. 4) The semigroup S contains no free subsemigroup of rank two. 5) The semigroup S is a subsemigroup of E(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}_\infty = \mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ denote the Riemann sphere, and consider rational functions $\mathbb{C}_\infty\to\mathbb{C}_\infty$ of degree at least two under the operation of composition $\circ$. A rational function $P$ of degree at least two is called special if either $P$ is conjugate (by a Möbius transformation) to $z^{\pm n}$ or to a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$, or $P$ is a Lattès map (induced from an endomorphism of an elliptic curve). For a non-special rational function $P$ of degree at least two, define
$$E(P) = \{A : A \text{ is a rational function of degree} \ge 2 \text{ that commutes with an iterate of } P\text{ within an appropriate iterative structure}\},$$
i.e. the semigroup of rational maps $A$ for which there exist iterates with $A\circ P^{\circ n} = P^{\circ m}\circ A$ for some $n,m\ge 1$ (the "semigroup of maps semiconjugate to $P$").

A semigroup $S$ (under composition) is called right amenable if there exists a finitely additive probability measure $\mu$ on the subsets of $S$ that is invariant under right translations $s\mapsto s\circ a$ for all $a\in S$. The semigroup $S$ is called right reversible if for every $A,B\in S$ one has $S\circ A \cap S\circ B \ne \emptyset$. A free subsemigroup of rank two in $S$ is a subsemigroup isomorphic to the free semigroup on two generators.

Let $S$ be a semigroup (under composition) of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Prove or disprove that the following five conditions are equivalent:

(1) $S$ is right amenable.
(2) $S$ is right reversible.
(3) For every $A,B\in S$ there exist integers $k,l\ge 1$ such that
$$A^{\circ 2k} = A^{\circ k}\circ B^{\circ l}\quad\text{and}\quad B^{\circ 2l} = B^{\circ l}\circ A^{\circ k}.$$
(4) $S$ contains no free subsemigroup of rank two.
(5) There exists a non-special rational function $P$ of degree at least two such that $S$ is a subsemigroup of $E(P)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture of equivalence of these five conditions for semigroups of rational functions containing a non-special element appears to remain open in full generality. Partial results are available: every subsemigroup of E(P) for non-special P of degree at least two is known to be amenable (and power-twisted), and analogues have been proved for polynomial semigroups and certain semigroups of formal power series, but the full equivalence (especially the implication from right amenability or absence of a rank-two free subsemigroup to membership in some E(P)) is not established in the rational case.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions (Pakovich)
status_evidence.snippet: Every subsemigroup S of E(P), where P is a non-special rational function of degree at least two, is amenable / power twisted.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results toward the conjecture: amenability of subsemigroups of E(P) is established, but the converse direction characterizing all right amenable semigroups remains open.

status_evidence.title: On amenability and measure of maximal entropy for semigroups of rational maps: II
status_evidence.snippet: Studies right amenability for semigroups of rational maps; related open questions about characterizing right-amenable semigroups remain.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of right amenable semigroups of rational functions is an active open area with only partial answers.
